title: High-Throughput Cardiotoxicity Screening Using Mature Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocyte Monolayers
protocol: Warm all reagents to room temperature and rehydrate MECM plates with Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS) or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) containing calcium and magnesium for 1 h prior to cardiomyocyte plating (200 μL of buffer per well).
Wash the MECM plates twice with HBSS or PBS containing calcium and magnesium for 1 h prior to cardiomyocyte plating (200 μL of buffer per well) and keep wells hydrated.
Prepare a 37 °C water bath.
Remove cardiomyocyte tubes from liquid nitrogen tank, transfer to dry ice, and slightly open tube caps to release pressure.
Reseal the tube caps and place them in the water bath to thaw for 4 min.
Spray the tubes containing thawed cells with 70% ethanol before opening.
Transfer the cells into 15 mL conical tubes using a 1 mL pipette.
Drip 8 mL of plating medium slowly into the tube, agitating it each time 1 mL is added.
Wash the cryovial with 1 mL of plating medium using a 1 mL glass pipette.
Slowly drip the wash into the 15 mL conical tube containing cells.
Centrifuge the tubes at ~300 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of plating medium.
Remove an aliquot and perform live cell counting with a hemocytometer.
Add additional plating medium to obtain 7.5 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Dispense 100 μL of cell suspension per well of an MECM-coated 96-well plate using a multichannel pipette.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 2 days prior to changing the medium to maintenance medium (200 µL/well).
Change the maintenance medium on day 5 after thawing.
Perform EP assays on day 7 or later as described previously.
Change the medium every other day when extending cell culture.
Warm EDTA solution, HBSS without calcium and magnesium (HBSS--), and mouse ECM-coated 6-well plates to room temperature.
Mark the differentiated colonies by phase-contrast microscopy and aspirate/ablate.
Wash each well with 1 mL of HBSS--. Perform two washes in wells containing >10 differentiation spots.
Aspirate the HBSS-- and add 1 mL of EDTA solution to each well. Incubate the plates for up to 5 min at 37 °C.
Check the plates after 3 min and look for translucent white, visible colonies.
Aspirate the EDTA solution and add 1 mL to a single well.
Dislodge the cells with 2 mL of hiPSC medium by pipetting the suspension up and down repeatedly using a 10 mL glass pipette. Transfer the cell suspension to a collection tube.
Repeat the aspiration and dislodging with subsequent wells.
Count the stem cells and adjust the volume to plate 8.0 × 10^5 cells/well.
Culture the cells on hiPSC medium (2 mL/well) until the stem cells reach 90% confluence (this time is referred from now on as D0).
Prepare 2 mL of basal differentiation medium supplemented with 4 µM of CHIR99021.
Wash each well of a 6-well plate of stem cells with 1 mL of HBSS per well.
Replace the HBSS with basal differentiation medium supplemented with 4 µM of CHIR99021.
Do nothing on D1.
Prepare basal differentiation medium supplemented with 4 µM of IWP4 on D2.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of IWP4-supplemented basal differentiation medium per well on D2.
Do nothing for ventricular-specific differentiation on D3.
For atrial-specific differentiation, aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of basal medium supplemented with 4 µM of IWP4 and 1 µM retinoic acid (RA) solution per well on D3.
Aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of basal medium per well for ventricular differentiation on D4.
For atrial differentiation, aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of basal medium supplemented with 1 µM RA solution per well on D4.
Do nothing on D5.
Aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of basal medium per well (for both atrial and ventricular differentiation) on D6.
Do nothing on D7.
Aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of cardiomyocyte maintenance medium on D8.
Change the medium every other day until cell separation, or follow a chronic drug exposure plan.
Aspirate the cell culture medium and wash each well with 1 mL of HBSS-- for MACS purification.
Dissociate the cells by adding 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin/EDTA and incubating at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 10 min.
Resuspend and singularize the cells in each well with 2 mL of plating medium to inactivate the trypsin/EDTA.
Collect the cells from six wells into a 50 mL conical tube with a 70 µm strainer.
Wash the strainer with 3 mL of plating medium.
Count the collected cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at ~300 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Wash the pellet with 20 mL of ice-cold MACS separation buffer.
Centrifuge again at ~300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 80 µL of cold MACS separation buffer per 5 × 106 cells.
Add 20 µL of cold non-cardiomyocyte depletion cocktail (human) per 5 × 106 cells to the resuspended cells.
Incubate on ice for 10 min while gently mixing.
Wash the cell sample by adding 4 mL of cold MACS separation buffer per 5 × 106 cells.
Centrifuge the washed sample at ~300 × g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 80 µL of cold MACS separation buffer per 5 × 106 cells again.
Add 20 µL of cold anti-biotin microbeads per 5 × 106 cells to the resuspended cells.
Incubate for 10 min on ice while gently mixing.
Place positive depletion columns (fitted with the 30 µm pre-separation filters) on the MACS separator and place labeled 15 mL collection tubes below each column, one for every 5 × 106 cells.
Prime each column with 3 mL of cold MACS separation buffer.
Mix antibody-treated cell suspension with 2 mL of MACS separation buffer per 5 × 106 cells.
Add the mixture to the prepared columns without centrifuging.
Add 2 mL of MACS separation buffer to each column.
Collect the flowthrough until 12 mL of cardiomyocyte suspension is collected.
Centrifuge the cardiomyocytes at ~300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Suspend the cardiomyocytes in 1 mL of plating medium.
Count the cells to determine concentration.
Adjust the volume to the desired seeding density.
Plate the purified cardiomyocytes on MECM 96-well plates (7.5 × 10^5 cells/well).
Prepare VSD solution by adding 1 µL of VSD dye per mL of HBSS and 10 µL of loading adjuvant per mL of HBSS.
Aspirate the cardiomyocyte maintenance medium.
Replace with 100 µL of VSD or CSF per well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate the cells for 30 min in the cell culture incubator.
Remove dyes and replace with assay medium or HBSS.
Equilibrate at 37 °C for baseline data acquisition using optical mapping device.
Use four doses of a compound for cardiotoxicity testing in 96-well plates, including the clinical effective therapeutic plasma concentration and concentrations above and below it.
Plate 7.5 × 10^4 CMs per well of each 96-well plate to form confluent monolayers using plating medium.
Switch to cardiomyocyte maintenance medium after 48 h in plating medium.
Add recombinant adenovirus for expressing GCaMP6m (AdGCaMP6m) at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) = 5 on day 4.
Remove AdGCaMP6m medium and replace with fresh RPMI+B27 on day 5.
Observe the CMs using microscopy or the optical mapping imager on day 7 to visualize spontaneous contractions and corresponding calcium transients.
Transfer 96-well plates of mature hiPSC-CM monolayers expressing GCaMP6m to the optical mapping imager from the incubator for baseline data acquisition on day 7 or later.
Return the plates of CMs to the tissue culture incubator following electrophysiology data acquisition, for measurements at a subsequent time point.
Apply medications using at least four doses per medication and at least six wells per dose after baseline recordings.
Equilibrate the medications on the cells for at least 30 minutes prior to data collection.
Warm the well temperature to approximately 37 °C before and during data acquisition.
Add isoproterenol (500 nM) to every well following baseline recordings of an entire plate to enable robust drug response data.
Quantify the effects of isoproterenol on monolayer beat rate, contraction amplitude (calcium transient amplitude), and calcium transient duration.
Turn on the optical mapping device camera, transilluminator, and plate heater.
Open the acquisition software and determine the file saving location.
Position the plate on the plate heater in the front drawer.
Acquire a dark frame by clicking on the Dark Frame button.
Select Duration (10-30 s) and Frame Rate of Acquisition (e.g., 100 fps; 250 fps for higher temporal resolution).
Click Start Acquisition.
Open the analysis software and select either Browse for a single file or Tile Multiple to reconstruct a plate in the Import/Filter tab.
Select Parameter Mode (APD or CaTD) and enter Distance per Pixel.
Use the Well Wizard to determine the wells' location in the image.
Click Process Save to move to the next tab.
Open the ROIs (regions of interest) tab and choose to draw the ROIs Manually, Automatically, or Not Use ROIs at all.
After selecting the ROIs, click the Process/Save button to move to the next step.
Check the Hide Wells and Only Show Filtered boxes to visualize the ROIs.
Open the Analysis tab and select each Well or ROI to confirm the Accuracy of Automatic Beat Detection.
Add or Remove Beats from the traces by pressing Add Beat/ Save Beats or selecting an Individual Beat and pressing Delete on the keyboard.
Optionally, use the Average Heat Maps feature to create heatmaps of selected parameters for the plate.
Click on the Time-Space Plot button in the Analysis tab.
Visualize data for each well or ROI.
Proceed to the Export tab and select File Format.
Press Export and create a folder for the data to be exported to.
Open data files.
Run the chosen statistical analysis routine.
